title: From kubectl apply to a running container
prompt: You run `kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml` for notes-api with 3 replicas on a fresh cluster. Put what happens next in order.
hints: Nothing happens anywhere until the object is stored.
A Deployment doesn't create Pods itself; it manages something that does.
A Pod has to be assigned to a node before any kubelet will act on it.
explanation: kubectl sends the object to the API server, which validates it and stores it in etcd. The Deployment controller sees a new Deployment and creates a ReplicaSet; the ReplicaSet controller creates three Pod objects. The scheduler assigns each unscheduled Pod to a node. The kubelet on each chosen node pulls the image and starts the containers, then reports the Pod's status back through the API server. Each step is a separate component reacting to a change it watched for.

items.send: kubectl sends the Deployment to the API server
items.store: The API server validates it and stores it in etcd
items.rs: The Deployment controller creates a ReplicaSet
items.pods: The ReplicaSet controller creates three Pod objects
items.schedule: The scheduler assigns each Pod to a node
items.start: Each node's kubelet pulls the image and starts the containers
items.report: The kubelet reports Pod status back to the API server
